NOTES.text:
Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will continue with module seven on functional materials, that is, polymers.

Key details

  • Today we will talk about another polymer composite that is carbon fiber.
  • We talk about the synthesis, properties and applications and finally we will look at the composite of carbon fiber which is known as carbon fiber reinforced polymer.
  • What are carbon fibers?
  • Basically, they are fibers which are made mostly of carbon atoms, and the diameter is just about 5 to 10 micrometers.
  • When you compare this diameter with the human hair, as you can see in the picture here, the human hair is much thicker as compared to the carbon fiber.
  • On polymerization is known as polyacrylonitrile.
  • So now the next step, how we are going to use this polyacrylonitrile to get the carbon fiber.
  • So here again the first step would be polymerization which I mentioned just now.
  • So all these acrylonitrile molecules are going to be placed like this because it is renal cyanide.
  • The polymerization will always take across take place across the double bond.
  • So you can see the chain has got formed because of the opening of this double bond.
  • So that is the first step which is.
  • Now the next step is we need to cyclize it.
  • Remember that we want a graphite like structure.
  • So the next step would be cyclization that is done at a low temperature.
  • Cyclization process there will be a bond which will be formed between this carbon and this nitrogen.
  • Up and you get a bond getting formed between C and N, and here it will be left with double bond.
  • That's exactly what you can see in this picture, and that will result in a cyclic molecules, and therefore that is called as the cyclization process.
  • Polymer now has become cyclic is constituted of cyclic chains, or you can see here cyclic rings, and these are in the form of a chain.
  • So now the next step would be.
  • I want a double bond here.
  • Because we want to go towards a graphite like structure.
  • I want a double bond here.
  • How do I get it?
  • That is done by the oxidative treatment.
  • This is the cyclization, and the third step would be oxidative treatment, which is done at a higher temperature.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

This is done at a higher temperature.

Key details

  • Obviously, it is treated with oxygen and water molecule will be eliminated, and here basically we are removing hydrogen.
  • Hydrogen that is unsaturation now came up.
  • we are basically causing oxidation of this.
  • this small this chain polymer over here.
  • So now the next step is the most important step where we are going to go towards the graphite like structure.
  • Of course the last step would be where you remove all other elements except carbon because we want a graphite like structure that is made of carbon.
  • So graffiti is the final process and that is done at a very high temperature and in an inert atmosphere and inert atmosphere because you're treating it taking the fibre to such a high temperature, so it will it'll become inflammable, it may catch fire.
  • We got some unsaturation in these positions by oxidative treatment and finally we heated it and we got the ribbon like structures joined together to give you this type of structure and finally when it is graffitized, that's called graphitization at a very high temperature.
  • Then we get what we call as the carbon fiber.
  • If you remember graphite is made up of it, it has a layer structure and.
  • These chains between these layers actually there is a there is just Vanderwall force of attraction.
  • But we do that carbon fiber is one of the strongest material.
  • In graphite we have very regular pattern these lay of carbon they are just one below the other and because they're all sp2 hybridized so we have layers like this and these chains between the chains is just one wall force and the these chains can slip against each other.
  • It is known as a turbostratic arrangement.
  • What is that?
  • These sheets of carbon fiber are half as a leaf folded or crumpled together.
  • They are all folded and crumpled so as a result that slipping of chains is not possible and this is known as the turbostratic arrangement and that gives the carbon fiber a good strength.
  • Say that it is also biocompatible.
  • It is a fiber which is biocompatible and it has a low coefficient of thermal expansion.
  • Of course, the most used property is high strength to weight ratio.

Core explanation · 10:00–14:59

What would be the applications?

Key details

  • It's very clear such a strong material we have.
  • It is used in aerospace, road and marine transport, it is used in sporting goods and medical applications in prostesis surgery.
  • Ligamentary repair of those.
  • Because it is biocompatible.
  • Then we also have automobile goods, novel tooling, casings and bases for electronic equipment, EMI and RF shielding brushes.
  • But what we have learnt now is about the advantages.
  • Of course, it is very expensive due to the large ex energy expenditure.
  • Which are going to use carbon fiber, especially where a lot of strength is required.
  • And one more disadvantage would be volatile byproducts are formed.
  • We know that when we make a composite, there has to be a fiber that is the carbon fiber, and the matrix is the epoxy resin.
  • That is how it is getting the strength.
  • Of course, we know light weight and high strength to weight ratio, low coefficient of thermal expansion.
  • But one new property which has come here and very important is the high electrical conductivity.
  • Because we know it has a graphite like structure and we know that graphite.
  • is conducting in nature.
  • So because of that we find that it has high electrical conductivity.
  • So in the next class now we are going to talk about a new class of polymers which are called conducting.
  • Polymers so far polymers were always thought of as insulators, but yes, there is a class of polymers which are which can actually conduct as good as that of the metal, and these are known as conducting polymers.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Like for example, H Cn could be formed when we are making carbon fiber from polyacrylonitrile.
